findings.title: Hand-rolled XML highscore parser consumes unauthenticated plain-HTTP response: client DoS and on-screen content spoofing
findings.entry_point: HTTP GET response body of http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.xml (fetched at line 81-83, plain HTTP, no signature/validation), pulled every time a game ends when canConnect() && main.isOriginal() (ApoDefenceGame.java:400-405 and 426-431)
findings.sink: makeEntity(String) lines 95-115: indexOf/substring slicing plus Integer.parseInt (lines 102-103, 108-109); results rendered via ApoDefenceHighscoreEntity.render -> Graphics.drawString (ApoDefenceHighscoreEntity.java:57-69)
findings.data_path: URL.openStream() (line 83) -> Scanner(useDelimiter "\\Z").next() slurps whole body (line 87) -> private makeEntity(String) strips \t/\n then loops on <person>/<nickname>/<level>/<map>/<point> markers -> addEntity(name,map,level,points) -> render() draws attacker strings on the win/lose screen
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker controls daporius.drition.net DNS/host or sits on-path (cleartext HTTP, so any LAN/WiFi/gateway MITM works): (a) serve '<person><nickname>a</nickname><level>zzz</level>' -> Integer.parseInt('zzz') throws NumberFormatException, or '<person>' with no '</person>' -> substring(idx,-1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException; the exception escapes think() (ApoDefenceGame.java:405/431) into ApoDefenceTimer.run(), killing the java.util.Timer thread -> game freezes. (b) serve well-formed rows with nickname 'PWNED' mapped to the victim's current map -> fake leaderboard rows are painted, highlighted red as the player's own placement.
findings.preconditions: Player finishes a map (win or loss) with default/original option settings (isOriginal(), ApoDefenceOptions.java:81-88) and canConnect()'s plain-HTTP probe of http://home.arcor.de/newbielein/test.gif succeeds (line 63-64) - trivially true for a MITM who serves any decodable GIF. Endpoints appear long-dead, so in practice the attacker must be on-path or control DNS.
findings.validation_plan: Add '127.0.0.1 daporius.drition.net' to /etc/hosts, run python3 -m http.server 80 serving highscore.xml containing '<person><nickname>x</nickname><level>NaN</level></person>'; play Original_First until win/loss screen; observed result: NumberFormatException stack trace and permanently frozen game loop (timer thread dead). Repeat with valid XML using nickname PWNED/map Original_First to confirm spoofed red-highlighted leaderboard row renders.

findings.title: Score submission over cleartext HTTP where the only 'protection' is iterated Base64 (Base64Coder misnamed Encrypt) plus a day-of-month check
findings.code_excerpt: String url = "http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php?"; String getUrl = "name=" + baseName + "&map=" + baseMap + "&level=" + baseLevel + "&points=" + basePoints + "&cor=" + day;
findings.entry_point: ApoDefenceGame.mouseReleased 'Upload' button handler (ApoDefenceGame.java:775-783) sends nicknameField.getText(), level name from the loaded .defence file, waves and points - all client-controlled
findings.sink: HttpURLConnection GET to http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php (lines 198-203), accepted server-side as a score entry
findings.data_path: send(name,map,level,points) (166) -> ApoDefenceHighscoreEncrypt.encodeString applied 3x to name, 4x to map, 2x to level/points/day (168-189) - ApoDefenceHighscoreEncrypt.java:61-63 is verbatim public-domain Base64Coder (comment lines 4-8), zero cryptography - concatenated into URL (191-195) -> con.getInputStream() (203)
findings.attack_scenario: (1) Forgery without playing: anyone computes the encoding offline (e.g. points=999999 quintuple-Base64) and curls the URL - the 'cor' parameter is just double-Base64 of the day-of-month, guessable forever. (2) On-path tampering: because it is cleartext HTTP, a MITM rewrites the points parameter in flight. (3) Gate bypass: the only client-side guard is isOriginal() (ApoDefenceOptions.java:81-88), which compares live settings to money/towerCount/waves read back from the user-editable .defence file itself (ApoDefenceOptionsGeneral.java:148-166), so crafting a level file with generous values makes 'original' true. Amplifier: the map value sent is the level FILE NAME (loadSave.getLevel(), ApoDefenceGame.java:777; ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:154) taken unsanitized from disk, so a distributed level named 'X&points=<forged>&...' injects parameters into the GET.
findings.preconditions: For forgery: nothing but network access to the (historical) endpoint; for MITM: position on path; for the gate: ability to hand the victim a crafted .defence level or edit their own.
findings.validation_plan: Replicate encoding in python: b64(b64(b64('Cheater')))=name, b64^4('Original_First')=map, b64^2('40')=level, b64^5('999999')=points, b64^2(str(datetime.day))=cor; curl 'http://daporius.drition.net/highscore.php?name=..&map=..&..' while tcpdump shows the plaintext request; if the server were resurrected, re-fetching highscore.xml would list Cheater/999999. Offline proof: decode any captured legitimate request with 5x base64-decode to recover exact fields.

findings.title: Level-file header ints drive unbounded allocations (new int[y][x], BufferedImage(x*32,y*32), count-driven object loops)
findings.code_excerpt: this.x = data.readInt(); this.y = data.readInt(); this.aPlayground = new int[this.y][this.x];
findings.entry_point: .defence binary level file: chosen via JFileChooser (ApoDefenceGame.setLoad, ApoDefenceGame.java:347-370, opened from Options->Load, ApoDefenceOptions.java:170-172; editor equivalent ApoDefenceEditorGame.java:306-335), or auto-loaded levels/Original_First.defence at startup (ApoDefenceGame.java:176) - i.e., any downloadable/shared user level
findings.sink: new int[this.y][this.x] (line 159); downstream new BufferedImage(this.x * 32, this.y * 32,...) (ApoDefenceGame.makeNewXAndY, ApoDefenceGame.java:225); unbounded count loops: enemyWay size (line 177-183) and enemies size (lines 192-196) allocate one object per declared int with no cap
findings.data_path: readLevel(fileName) (145) -> raw DataInputStream.readInt x2 (156-157) straight into array dimensions; no upper bound, no sanity check vs file length; negative values yield NegativeArraySizeException, huge values OutOfMemoryError; neither is IOException so they propagate uncaught through setLoad to the caller
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker distributes an attractive 'custom map' .defence whose first 8 bytes are 0x3B9AC9FF twice (or simply 2000000000/-1): victim opens it via Load -> immediate NegativeArraySizeException/OOME crash; a subtler file (e.g. 60000x60000) passes int[] allocation attempts and dies allocating the 1.92M-pixel-x32 BufferedImage, or declares enemyWay size 0x7FFFFFFF so the loop at 177-183 exhausts heap from a ~30-byte file.
findings.preconditions: Victim loads the attacker-supplied .defence file (classic malicious-user-content path for this genre); no other conditions.
findings.validation_plan: Write a file: bytes 0-7 big-endian 1000000000,1000000000, append junk, save as evil.defence; launch game, Options->Load, select evil.defence; observed result: NegativeArraySizeException (negative variant) or OutOfMemoryError (large variant) with ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel in the trace. Second file with enemyWay-size field 0x7FFFFFFF confirms heap exhaustion from a tiny file.

findings.title: UTF string from level file used as classpath resource name for underground image - reliable crash, but no filesystem traversal
findings.entry_point: imageString field (DataInputStream.readUTF) of a user-supplied .defence level file (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:185)
findings.sink: ApoDefenceImage.getPic -> getImage: Class.getResource(BildName) then ImageIO.read(...) (lines 63-110); dereferenced without null check at img.getWidth() line 108
findings.data_path: readLevel readUTF (ApoDefenceLoadSave.java:185) -> getLoadSave().getImageString() -> ApoDefenceGame.restart() lines 1069-1073 (this.image.getPic(this.imageString,false)); editor twin at ApoDefenceEditorGame.java:325-329 -> getResource resolves against classloader roots only; missing resource returns null -> ImageIO.read(null) throws IllegalArgumentException (only IOException is caught at line 104), or NPE at line 108
findings.attack_scenario: Craft a .defence with imageString '/images/nope.png': on load the game throws IllegalArgumentException/NPE during restart() and dies - a second crash vector bundled with the same malicious-level distribution as ApoDefence-03. IMPORTANT negative result: '../../etc/passwd' style values do NOT escape the classpath (getResource never resolves arbitrary filesystem/remote paths here), so this is not a file-disclosure bug; marking that angle explicitly unreachable/theoretical.
findings.preconditions: Victim loads the crafted level file; crash only - no code execution, no read-outside-classpath.
findings.validation_plan: Take a working Original_First.defence, locate the writeUTF imageString segment ('/images/underground.png' visible as readable string), replace with '/images/zz.png' keeping lengths consistent; open via Load; observed result: IllegalArgumentException ('input == null!') or NPE at ApoDefenceImage.java:108 immediately after selection. Try '../../../etc/passwd' to confirm it also merely crashes (null resource), proving no traversal.

categories_checked_and_absent: remote_code_loading - no ClassLoader/defineClass/System.load anywhere (repo-wide grep, 0 hits)
untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream/XML decoder; level format is primitive DataInputStream reads only
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords/tokens/API keys in source
legacy_sandbox_assumption - pure desktop JFrame app (ApoDefenceMain.main, line 122-125); no applet/JNLP entry point, no SecurityManager assumptions
path_traversal - only file access is JFileChooser-selected level paths; the one non-chooser path (imageString) provably cannot leave the classpath (see ApoDefence-04)
MessageDigest/MD5-based weak hashing - absent in this variant; its role is played by iterated Base64 (ApoDefence-02)
notes: Layout quirk: the source tree is nested under Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoDefence/ApoDefence/ inside the variant root; all 67 files are .java (no build artifacts/resources committed). This variant does NOT use the corpus-typical apo-games.de endpoints: highscore traffic targets daporius.drition.net (author's personal host) with a connectivity oracle at home.arcor.de/newbielein/test.gif (ApoDefenceHighscore.java:64,82,191) - all long-defunct, so network findings are on-path/hijack scenarios today. No savegame/replay/.cheat/.mar/.skunk formats exist here; the only persistent artifact is the editor-produced .defence level format. ApoDefenceSounds.java is dead code (referenced only by its own main(), lines 32-66). game/ApoDefenceFileFilter.java is a near-verbatim clone of the root ApoDefenceFileFilter.java (diff: package/class visibility only) - intra-variant duplication consistent with the clone-and-own hypothesis; the LoadSave/Image/Highscore/Base64Coder infrastructure mirrors sibling variants modulo the apo-prefix rename, hence shared_component=true throughout. The isOriginal() highscore gate comparing against attacker-writable level-file values (ApoDefenceOptionsGeneral.java:156-167) is worth tracking across variants as a recurring design flaw.
